terms.gloss: things to frighten with: a scarecrow, a bugbear
evidence: Liv. 34.11.7: nūllīs minīs, nūllīs terriculīs sē mōtōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From terreō; very rare, and in Livy of empty threats (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens gives the singular terriculum for a scarecrow.

terms.gloss: a terror; a thing set up to scare
evidence: Hor. S. 1.8.3–4: fūrum aviumque maxima formīdō
terms.comment: Horace’s garden Priapus calls himself “the great terror of thieves and birds”.

phrases.latin: deus inde ego, fūrum aviumque maxima formīdō
phrases.english: so I am a god, the great terror of thieves and birds

sources: Lewis & Short: terricula · Lewis & Short: formido
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. scarecrow.
